title: How to tell a customer their AC needs to be replaced
summary: Paste what you found on the visit into ChatGPT and get a calm explanation that the AC should be replaced. Check the facts and the price before you send it.

tests.prompt:
You help an HVAC technician explain that an air conditioner should be replaced. Write one calm message. Draft only. Do not send it.

Fill in these details. If a line is blank, write UNKNOWN and do not guess.

Customer name: [CUSTOMER NAME]
Job address: [JOB ADDRESS]
What's wrong with the current unit: [PROBLEM]
Age of the current unit, if known: [AGE]
Repair option, if there is one: [REPAIR OPTION]
Why replacement is recommended: [WHY REPLACE]
Recommended system: [SYSTEM]
Price: [PRICE]
What's included: [INCLUDED]
What's not included: [NOT INCLUDED]
Timeline: [TIMELINE]
Your name and business: [YOUR NAME]
Your phone: [YOUR PHONE]
Email or text: [CHANNEL]

Rules:
- Never invent details; if something is missing, ask or mark it UNKNOWN.
- Do not scare the customer. Do not say the unit will fail this week, or that it is unsafe, unless those words are already in [PROBLEM] or [WHY REPLACE].
- Do not invent a SEER rating, a brand, a rebate, or a financing plan.
- If [REPAIR OPTION] has a price, include it fairly so they can compare. If it is blank, do not invent a repair price.
- Do not change [PRICE]. Copy it exactly.
- Keep the tone steady and clear, like a technician at the kitchen table. No pressure and no "today only" language.

Output format:
Return these headings only:
Channel
Subject (NONE if this is a text)
Message (200 words or fewer for email, 100 words or fewer for a text)
The situation
Repair option (or NONE)
Replacement recommendation
Price and what's included
What's not included
Next step
Facts used
Unknown

setup.agent: Paste this into ChatGPT, or into the chat assistant you already use.
steps: After the visit, write the customer name, address, what's wrong, the age if you know it, a repair option if one exists, why you recommend replacement, the system, and the price.
Add what's included and not, the timeline, your name, phone, and whether this is an email or a text.
Open ChatGPT, paste the ChatGPT prompt, and replace every [BRACKET]. Type UNKNOWN if you do not have a fact yet.
Read the draft beside your notes. Confirm the problem, the price, and that it does not invent a rebate, a brand detail, or a scare line.
Paste the message into email or a text and send it yourself. Offer to walk them through questions on the phone.
setup.approvalStep: You check the diagnosis, the replacement price, and any repair option against your notes, then you send the message yourself.
failureModes: The draft says the unit is unsafe or will fail immediately when you did not say that. Soften it to match your diagnosis.
A rebate, tax credit, or financing offer appears that you did not include. Delete it.
The replacement price or the system size does not match your quote. Put your figures back in.
A repair option you offered is left out or understated. If you gave a repair price, it should appear fairly.

faq.q: What if there is no reasonable repair option?
faq.a: Leave [REPAIR OPTION] blank so the draft does not invent one. Explain why replacement is the recommendation, using only what you found on the visit.

faq.q: Should I mention rebates or tax credits?
faq.a: Only if you have checked the current program and typed it into the details. Do not let the draft invent a rebate or a dollar amount.

faq.q: The homeowner is upset. How direct should I be?
faq.a: Be clear and calm. State what you found, the options, and the prices. Do not pile on fear. Offer a phone call as the next step so they can ask questions.

job: Paste visit notes and get a calm explanation that an AC should be replaced, with the price and any repair option.
who: HVAC technicians and shop owners who need to recommend a replacement without scaring the homeowner or burying the price.

example.scenario: A 16-year-old central AC has a failing compressor. Repair is possible but the technician recommends replacement.
example.input:
Customer name: Casey Reed
Job address: 3 Harbor View
What's wrong with the current unit: Compressor is failing, unit is short-cycling and not cooling the upstairs
Age of the current unit, if known: 16 years
Repair option, if there is one: Compressor replacement for $2,400, with no labor warranty on a 16-year unit
Why replacement is recommended: The unit is 16 years old, a compressor repair is a large share of a new system, and the coil is original
Recommended system: 3-ton central AC to match the current size, standard efficiency
Price: $7,850 installed
What's included: New outdoor unit, matching coil, startup, and haul-away of the old unit
What's not included: Duct repairs, a new thermostat, and electrical panel work
Timeline: One day on site, earliest the week of November 17
Your name and business: Casey at Fair Air
Your phone: 555-0190
Email or text: email
example.output:
Channel: email
Subject: AC options for 3 Harbor View

Message:
Hi Casey, this is Casey at Fair Air, following up on the visit at 3 Harbor View. The compressor on your 16-year-old central AC is failing, which is why the unit short-cycles and the upstairs is not cooling.

The situation: 16-year-old system, failing compressor, original coil.

Repair option: We can replace the compressor for $2,400. I can't offer a labor warranty on a 16-year unit.

Replacement recommendation: I recommend a new 3-ton central AC, the same size you have now, at standard efficiency. At this age, the compressor repair is a large share of a new system.

Price and what's included: $7,850 installed, including the new outdoor unit, a matching coil, startup, and haul-away of the old unit. We can do it in one day, earliest the week of November 17.

What's not included: Duct repairs, a new thermostat, and electrical panel work.

Next step: I can walk you through either option. Call or text me at 555-0190 when you want to talk it over.

Facts used: 3 Harbor View, 16 years, $2,400 repair, $7,850 replacement, 3-ton, week of November 17.
Unknown: none.
example.notes: Made-up equipment and prices, only to show a calm comparison of repair and replacement.
